title: Indonesia's new finance minister faces a test of delivery
gist: Indonesia's new finance minister Suahasil Nazara, a delivery-focused technocrat who frames his appointment as continuity, must make Prabowo's growth and social programs (notably the scandal-hit free meals MBG) work without eroding fiscal credibility. The 2027 budget cuts energy subsidies 6%, and the DTSEN database of 95.3 million households underpins a shift to targeted digital cash transfers trialled from early 2027.

insights.claim: Prabowo's priority programs are sound in principle but have suffered in execution; Suahasil's test is using Finance Ministry levers — funding, targeting, incentives, monitoring and fiscal discipline — to make them work.

insights.claim: The free nutritious meals (MBG) program has faced repeated food-poisoning incidents and the arrest of the former head of the National Nutrition Agency and senior officials in a corruption investigation; the Finance Ministry controls its budget and oversight though not its delivery.
insights.speaker: Hilman Palaon
insights.so_what: MBG is the flagship test of whether Prabowo's large social spending can be delivered without waste and scandal.

insights.claim: Suahasil takes a pragmatic view of energy subsidies, arguing fuel, cooking gas and electricity support stabilises prices, protects household purchasing power and gives businesses cost certainty, while better targeting requires reliable data and error-correction mechanisms.
